title: HCP — Import — payload
description: The request payload of the HCP 2.0-draft-3 Import operation (HCP 5.4.3, 5.4; `POST /v2/import` in HCP 9.4.11): a Management Client, at the Context Subject's direction, loads the entries of an HCP export into the Context Subject's instance. The members are HCP 5.4.3's request fields, with the access token moved into the payload. The outer document members (id, type, issuer, recipient, issuedAt, expiresAt, proof) are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

export.description: HCP `export`: an HCP export (HCP 5.4.1), with entries in any schema the provider accepts, including HCP v1 forms where it declares them in `accepts_entry_schemas` (HCP 5.4.3, 4.3, 19). Its shape is `ImportedExport`, HCP's own export shape, in which `options` is OPTIONAL, so that an export written to HCP's schema alone is accepted.

dryRun.description: HCP `dryRun`: if true, the provider reports the outcome for each entry and changes nothing (HCP 5.4.3). Absent or false means the import is carried out.

categoryMap.description: HCP `categoryMap`: for categories the provider does not hold, the category each is to be replaced by (HCP 5.4.3). Each key is a category used by entries in the export that the provider does not hold; its value is the category the provider holds that replaces it. That each key is itself a category is not checked by the schema. Each replacement is recorded as a `context.recategorized` audit event (HCP 5.4.3, 4.2.1). The maxProperties of 256 is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

accessToken.description: The Management Client's HCP access token (HCP 9.3), carried unchanged. HCP's HTTP binding sends it as a Bearer token; this member carries it in the document. The provider validates it exactly as over HTTP and treats it as opaque. The maxLength is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

Response.title: HCP — Import — response payload
Response.description: The HCP import result (HCP 5.4.3, 9.4.11): one outcome for each entry in the export. Failures of the import as a whole use trust-task-error, not this shape.

outcomes.description: HCP `outcomes`: one for each entry in the export (HCP 5.4.3). The maxItems matches the export's `entries` bound in hcp/_shared/0.1 and is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

dryRun.description: HCP `dryRun`, echoed: true where the request was a dry run and nothing was changed (HCP 9.4.11).

ext.description: Ecosystem-defined extension members per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Not an HCP member: HCP's import result is `outcomes` and `dryRun` only. This family defines one namespace here, `vnd.trusttasks.hcp-carriage`, the hcp/* Trust Task family's own extension, not HCP's: present only for a delegate's import, and only where the export holds a standing rule the delegate could not set with hcp/rules/set; its value MUST validate against the `HcpCarriageImportExtension` definition in this schema, pending HCP confirmation (question 40).

ImportedExport.description: An HCP export as hcp/import takes it (HCP 5.4.1, 5.4.3): HCP's own export shape, so that an export written to HCP's schema alone is accepted. It differs from the shared `Export` in hcp/_shared/0.1, which hcp/export returns, in two respects only, each as in HCP's own shape (question 42). First, `options`, and each member of it, is OPTIONAL here, where the shared `Export` requires them: where `options`, or `includeVersions` or `includeAudit` within it, is absent, it is unknown whether superseded versions or the audit log were requested, and the provider MUST NOT infer either, from the presence or absence of `versions` or `audit` or otherwise. Second, each event in `audit` is an `ImportedAuditEvent`, in which `entryId`, `relatedEntryId`, `purpose`, `purposeDescription` and `grantId` are OPTIONAL, where the shared `AuditEvent` requires them. Every other member is as in the shared `Export`, whose maxItems bounds these match: framework bounds, not HCP requirements. Open, as HCP's own shape is.

@context.description: The export's JSON-LD context, `https://hcp.example/contexts/v2` in HCP 2.0-draft-3 (HCP 5.4.1). As an array, at most 16 items: a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

schema.description: The export structure version, compared as an exact string (HCP 5.4.1, 1.7).

options.description: HCP `options`: the options requested (HCP 5.4.1). OPTIONAL, as in HCP's own shape. Absent means it is unknown whether `versions` or `audit` were requested, and the provider MUST NOT infer either.

entries.description: The current version of each entry exported, whatever its `record.status` (HCP 5.4.1). An export a provider writes carries each in the form of HCP 4.2 (see context-entry.schema.json `Entry`); an import accepts entries in any schema the importing provider accepts, including HCP v1 forms (HCP 5.4.3, 4.3), so items are left open here, as in HCP's own shape, and each is validated against the schema it names.

versions.description: Superseded versions, each in the form of HCP 4.2. Present only where requested (HCP 5.4.1). Whether they were requested is known only from `options.includeVersions` where present, never from this array.

delegations.description: The delegations made for the Context Subject, ended ones included, as a record. An import does not establish them (HCP 5.4.1, 17.2).

audit.description: The audit log, as events in the structure of HCP 8.2, each an `ImportedAuditEvent`, HCP's own audit-event shape. Present only where requested (HCP 5.4.1). Whether it was requested is known only from `options.includeAudit` where present, never from this array.

ImportedExportOptions.description: HCP `options` as hcp/import takes it (HCP 5.4.1): each member OPTIONAL, as in HCP's own shape, where the shared `ExportOptions` requires `includeVersions` and `includeAudit`. A member that is present says whether that option was requested; one that is absent leaves it unknown, and the provider MUST NOT infer it.

excludeDeleted.description: Entries whose `record.status` is `deleted` were omitted (HCP 5.4.1). Absent means unknown.

includeVersions.description: Superseded versions were requested (HCP 5.4.1). Absent means unknown.

includeAudit.description: The audit log was requested (HCP 5.4.1, 8.3). Absent means unknown.

ImportedAuditEvent.description: One audit event of an export as hcp/import takes it (HCP 8.2, 5.4.1, 5.4.3): HCP's own audit-event shape, so that an export written to HCP's schema alone is accepted. It differs from the shared `AuditEvent` in hcp/_shared/0.1, which hcp/export and hcp/audit/read return, in one respect only: `entryId`, `relatedEntryId`, `purpose`, `purposeDescription` and `grantId` are OPTIONAL here, as in HCP's own shape, where the shared `AuditEvent` requires each, a value or null (question 42). Where one is absent, it is unknown what the exporting provider recorded for it, and the provider MUST NOT read the absence as null. Every other member is as in the shared `AuditEvent`, whose bounds these match: framework bounds, not HCP requirements. Open, as HCP's own shape is.

eventType.description: The event type, one of those HCP 8.1 lists. Left open, as HCP's own shape leaves it. The minLength and maxLength are framework bounds, not HCP requirements.

timestamp.description: When the event occurred. HCP's member name (HCP 8.2), carried verbatim.

entryId.description: The entry concerned, by its `id`, or null where the event concerns none (HCP 8.2). OPTIONAL, as in HCP's own shape; absent means unknown.

relatedEntryId.description: For conflict events, the authoritative entry (or the other entry where neither or both are authoritative); null for every other event type (HCP 8.2). OPTIONAL, as in HCP's own shape; absent means unknown.

categories.description: The categories concerned (HCP 8.2). The maxItems is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

purpose.description: The purpose code stated, or null where none was (HCP 8.2, 6.1.5.2). OPTIONAL, as in HCP's own shape; absent means unknown. The maxLength is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

purposeDescription.description: The stated task, or null where none was stated (HCP 8.2). OPTIONAL, as in HCP's own shape; absent means unknown. The maxLength is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

grantId.description: The grant concerned, or null where the event concerns none (HCP 8.2). OPTIONAL, as in HCP's own shape; absent means unknown.

disclosed.description: Present on `context.read`: every entry the retrieval disclosed (HCP 8.2). A retrieval discloses at most 20 entries (HCP 7.2).

data.description: The members HCP 8.2 fixes for the event type. Implementations may add members, which are preserved and not interpreted (HCP 8.2, A.3).

HcpCarriageImportExtension.title: HCP — Import — vnd.trusttasks.hcp-carriage response extension
HcpCarriageImportExtension.description: The value of `ext["vnd.trusttasks.hcp-carriage"]` on the hcp/import response: the hcp/* Trust Task family's own extension, not an HCP member, so that the result itself stays HCP's. Present only for a delegate's import, and only where the export holds a standing rule the delegate could not set with hcp/rules/set (one naming no `categories`, or a category outside the delegation's scope), pending HCP confirmation (question 40). A Management Client that does not recognize the namespace ignores it (SPEC.md §4.5.1); it is informational and never marked critical.

rulesNotApplied.description: The `ruleId` of each standing rule in the export the delegate could not set, which the provider did not apply, or in a dry run would not apply (HCP 6.3, 17.4), pending HCP confirmation (question 40). The maxItems matches the export's `rules` bound in hcp/_shared/0.1 and is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

Outcome.description: The outcome for one entry of the export (HCP 5.4.3, 9.4.11). Open, as HCP's own import-result shape is. A `rejected` outcome carries `reason`: HCP 5.4.3 says "rejected, with the reason". That rule is not checked by the schema, because the registry's Rust generator does not support the conditional keywords it needs.

id.description: The entry's `id`, as the export carries it (HCP 5.4.3, 9.4.11).

outcome.description: `imported`; `converted`, a v1 entry converted under HCP 4.3; `skipped`, a deleted entry the provider chose not to carry (HCP 5.4.3 says the request chose, but its request has no member that chooses; pending HCP confirmation, question 34) or an exact duplicate of one held; or `rejected` (HCP 5.4.3). HCP's own values, carried verbatim.

reason.description: Why the entry was rejected, in words (HCP 5.4.3, 9.4.11), such as "id held with different content". It discloses nothing the condition forbids (HCP 5.5). The maxLength is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.
